title: Swift Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced Swift reference covering value semantics, optionals, collections, protocols, generics, errors, ARC, concurrency, actors, Sendable, testing, packages, performance, and API design.

subtopics.title: let, var & Value Semantics
subtopics.description: let prevents reassignment; var allows mutation. Structs, enums, and tuples are values; classes have reference identity.

subtopics.title: Optionals, guard & Pattern Matching
subtopics.description: Optional encodes absence. Bind safely with if let/guard let, chain when absence should propagate, and use switch for exhaustive domain logic.

callouts.title: Avoid Force Unwraps at Runtime Boundaries
callouts.text: Use ! only when an invariant is locally proven. Decode, validate, and fail with context for network, storage, and user input.

subtopics.title: Protocols, Extensions & Generics
subtopics.description: Protocols describe capabilities; extensions provide shared behavior; generics preserve concrete type information while any Protocol enables runtime existential storage.

codeBlocks.code:
protocol Repository: Sendable { associatedtype Model: Sendable; func find(_ id: UUID) async throws -> Model? }
func load<R: Repository>(from repo: R, id: UUID) async throws -> R.Model? { try await repo.find(id) }

subtopics.title: ARC, weak, unowned & Closures
subtopics.description: ARC manages class lifetimes. Break ownership cycles with weak when absence is valid and unowned only when the referenced object is guaranteed to outlive the reference.

callouts.title: Value Types Can Still Retain References
callouts.text: A struct containing a class or closure participates in that reference graph. Model ownership deliberately across callbacks and tasks.

subtopics.title: throws, Result & defer
subtopics.description: Use throws for synchronous/async propagation, Result when storing an outcome as data, and defer for scope-bound cleanup.

subtopics.title: Tasks, Actors & Sendable
subtopics.description: async/await suspends without blocking; task groups provide child ownership; actors isolate mutable state; Sendable marks values safe to cross isolation domains.

callouts.title: Cancellation Is Cooperative
callouts.text: Check cancellation in long loops, propagate it through dependencies, and avoid unstructured detached tasks unless lifetime ownership is explicit.

subtopics.title: Swift Package Manager, Testing & Performance
subtopics.description: Use focused modules, deterministic tests, dependency injection, Instruments, signposts, and allocation profiling before optimization.

subtopics.title: Actor Isolation, @MainActor & sending
subtopics.description: Swift 6 checks isolation crossings strictly. Put UI-facing state on MainActor, make transferred values Sendable, and use sending parameters/results when ownership is intentionally transferred between concurrency domains.

callouts.title: Do Not Silence Isolation with unchecked Sendable
callouts.text: @unchecked Sendable is a manual safety claim. Use it only after proving synchronization and documenting invariants; prefer immutable values, actors, or redesigned ownership.

subtopics.title: API & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Design expressive names, preserve value semantics, isolate shared mutation, model failure explicitly, and keep compatibility visible.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Enable strict concurrency checks, minimize force unwrap/cast, audit actor isolation, propagate cancellation, avoid retain cycles, redact secrets, test migrations, and profile release builds.
